subject: radiology
title: Liver-directed therapy: TACE and Y-90

steps.tx: **Transarterial chemoembolisation** delivers chemotherapy directly through the hepatic artery while embolic material reduces tumour blood flow. This approach bathes the tumour in drug while limiting exposure of the rest of the body. **DEB TACE** loads drug onto beads that release chemotherapy slowly after lodging inside tumour vessels. Clinicians select patients with preserved liver function and no portal invasion for safer treatment. **Post embolisation care** monitors pain, fever and liver failure after every treatment session carefully.
steps.say: Transarterial chemoembolisation provides chemotherapy directly through the hepatic artery to tumours. Embolic material reduces tumour blood flow while drug remains concentrated within liver. Drug loaded beads release chemotherapy slowly after lodging inside tumour vessels securely. Clinicians select preserved liver function because treatment can injure remaining liver.

steps.tx: This selective hepatic angiogram shows a **microcatheter tip** inside a feeding artery beside a dense hypervascular tumour blush. The blush marks the **hepatocellular carcinoma** target that clinicians plan to treat with transarterial chemoembolisation. Selective catheter position matters because it concentrates drug and embolic material inside tumour while sparing normal liver. In examinations, a round **tumour blush** after selective injection identifies the treatment target clearly.
steps.say: This angiogram shows a microcatheter inside a feeding artery beside tumour blush. The dense blush marks the hepatocellular carcinoma target planned for chemoembolisation treatment. Selective catheter position concentrates drug inside tumour while sparing normal liver tissue nearby. Candidates should identify tumour blush as the intended treatment target clearly.

vis.alt: Selective hepatic artery angiogram showing microcatheter tip and hypervascular hepatocellular carcinoma tumour blush.
vis.caption: Hepatic angiogram shows hypervascular tumour blush targeted for chemoembolisation. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Lipiodol TACE** carries a drug and oil emulsion into the tumour and remains visible on later computed tomography. **DEB beads** come in calibrated sizes, lodge predictably and release drug steadily inside the tumour bed. Selective segmental treatment spares normal liver while lobar treatment floods a larger territory and injures more tissue. Clinicians repeat sessions while tumours continue responding and the liver tolerates treatment without decompensation. Response assessment therefore combines tumour change with **liver tolerance** after each session.
steps.say: Lipiodol TACE carries drug and oil emulsion visibly into targeted liver tumours. Calibrated beads lodge predictably and release drug steadily inside the tumour bed. Selective segmental treatment helps spare normal liver while lobar treatment injures more tissue. Clinicians repeat sessions while tumours respond and liver function remains stable.

steps.tx: **Yttrium 90 radioembolisation** delivers beta radiation through microspheres that travel through arteries and lodge inside tumour beds. Clinicians perform a **lung shunt study** with technetium labelled albumin before treatment to limit pulmonary radiation dose. Gastrointestinal shunting towards stomach or duodenum can ulcerate those organs unless clinicians coil the responsible vessels first. **Radiation segmentectomy** gives a high curative dose to a small tumour bearing segment of liver. Careful mapping therefore protects lungs and bowel before therapeutic spheres are administered.
steps.say: Yttrium radioembolisation delivers beta radiation through arterial microspheres lodging in tumours. Clinicians perform lung shunt studies before treatment to limit pulmonary radiation dose. Gastrointestinal shunting can ulcerate stomach unless clinicians coil responsible vessels beforehand carefully. Radiation segmentectomy gives curative doses to small tumour bearing liver segments.

vis.alt: Diagram showing Y-90 radioembolisation in the liver, with arterial microsphere delivery to a tumor, and pre-treatment assessment for lung and GI shunts.
vis.caption: Y-90 radioembolisation: arterial microspheres deliver radiation to liver tumours

steps.tx: Treatment choice follows liver reserve, tumour distribution and whether the portal vein remains patent or invaded. TACE suits preserved livers with focal disease while **Yttrium 90 treatment** can still work when portal invasion exists. Either treatment can provide **bridging to transplant** by holding listed tumours within transplant criteria over time. **Downstaging** shrinks tumours that initially lie beyond criteria into an acceptable transplant range for selected patients. Systemic therapy follows when locoregional treatment alone cannot control disease across the liver.
steps.say: Treatment choice follows liver reserve, tumour distribution and portal vein patency status. TACE suits preserved livers with focal disease while Yttrium treatment tolerates invasion better. Bridging holds listed tumours within transplant criteria while patients await donor organs. Downstaging shrinks larger disease into transplant range for carefully selected patients.
